_note: What Genzo, the old rice farmer of Kaminoda, says when the farmer talks to him (Talk, README.md, Villagers): the first pick whose if holds names the lines, one of them by the day; gift_ lines answer a gift by its reaction. He has no hearts. Our own lines.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Hm? Still here. The paddies won't talk back, so I don't mind.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Go on, go on. A farmer standing still is a farmer losing light.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: The new one from the old farm below? I'm Genzo. These terraces were cut by my grandfather's grandfather.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Mind the dikes when you walk them. A broken dike is a whole summer's work.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Rain's the only hand I don't have to pay. Sit by the hearth a while, if you like.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Flooding the paddies this week. Listen at night: the frogs come back the same evening.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Seedlings go in a hand's width apart. My back says closer, my grandfather says no.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Weeds grow faster than rice in this heat. I pull them at dawn, before the sun's awake.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Heads are heavy and bowing. That's how you know rice is good: it gets humble.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Haru hangs the sheaves on the rack. Two weeks in the wind and they taste of it.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Paddies sleep in winter. So should I, but the straw won't braid itself.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: The well water here is cold all year. Drink some before you walk back down.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: The jizo by the lane? My wife sewed their bibs. I keep them red for her.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Now that's proper food. You were raised right, whoever raised you.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: For me? Hm. Thank you. I'll have it tonight.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: I'll find a use for it.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Sweet things and soft things... my teeth and I are too old for those.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: A stone. I pull those out of my paddies every spring. Take it back.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: One gift a day is plenty. Keep the rest for your own table.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Cooked it yourself? This is how my mother made it. Well. Nearly.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: A hot dish carried all the way up here. I won't let it go cold.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Hm. City cooking. I'll try it.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Too fancy for an old stomach. Thank you anyway.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: A daruma. I'll paint in the first eye tonight and wish for a good harvest.
